title: Product hygiene, single-use applicators and eye-area safety
audience: Mobile makeup artists who share a kit across several clients in a day
learningOutcomes: Select single-use or cleaned-and-disinfected tools for each product type
Keep products sealed, labelled and in date across a multi-client day
Identify the eye-area products that need extra care and the controls they need

instruction.heading: Why shared products cause harm
instruction.body: A product that has touched one client's skin can carry bacteria or other material to the next client. Dipping a used brush into a shared pot, or using a sponge on two faces, moves that material. The safest rule is that anything that touches the face and cannot be cleaned to a verified standard is single-use. Products that are decanted or used with the fingers need the same care.

instruction.heading: Cleaning and disinfection
instruction.body: Brushes that can be cleaned are washed after each client, dried flat and disinfected using a product whose label is followed for dilution and contact time. The contact time on the label is the time the product must stay wet. Disinfecting does not replace washing. A tool that is cracked, shedding or cannot be cleaned is removed from the kit. instruction.heading: Eye-area products
instruction.body: Eye products, lash adhesives and some pigments carry an extra risk of irritation. Read the safety data sheet for each product before first use, store adhesives as the sheet directs, and stop the service if the client reports stinging, watering or redness. Do not use a product in the eye area that is not labelled for that use.

procedure: Check each product's label and safety data sheet before it goes into the kit
Use single-use applicators for any product applied with a sponge, wand or spatula near the eyes or lips
Decant only into clean, labelled containers, and discard any decanted product at the end of the visit
Clean and disinfect reusable brushes after each client, using the label contact time
Close and store products between clients, and remove any product that is past its date or has been contaminated

workedExamples.situation: A therapist finishes a client on a shoot, then reaches for the same mascara wand to start the next client without changing it.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should happen to the mascara and the wand?
workedExamples.reasoning: The wand has touched one client's eye area and cannot be cleaned to a verified standard, so it is discarded. The mascara tube is set aside for that client and not used on the next. Single-use wands are used for each client.

equipmentAndPpe: Labelled spray bottles and decanting containers
Disinfectant approved for the kit, with the label available
Sealed storage box for products between clients
Safety data sheets for each product in the kit

commonErrors.error: Dipping a used brush back into a shared pot.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a clean single-use applicator for each dip, or decant a small amount to the client's own palette.

commonErrors.error: Treating disinfection as a replacement for washing.
commonErrors.prevention: Wash first, then disinfect with the label contact time.

commonErrors.error: Keeping products past their date because they still look usable.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the date on every product before each visit and remove expired items.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Eye-area products, lash adhesives and pigments need the safety data sheet read before first use. Stop the service if a client reports irritation.
Disinfectant concentrations and contact times are set by the product label. UNCONFIRMED: no official source has been fetched for this point in this draft. A reviewer must confirm it before approval.

qualityStandard: Each product in the kit has a current safety data sheet on hand
Single-use applicators are used for any product applied near the eyes or lips
Reusable tools are cleaned and disinfected after every client, with the time recorded
documentationEvidence: Product register with batch or open date and expiry date
Cleaning and disinfection log per visit
Record of discarded products and reason
summary: Shared products and reusable tools can carry material between clients
Single-use applicators are the default for face and eye-area products
Disinfection follows the label contact time and does not replace washing

knowledgeChecks.question: A mascara wand has touched one client's eye area. What is the correct action before the next client?
options: Wipe it on a tissue and reuse it
Discard it and use a new single-use wand
Dip it in disinfectant for a moment and reuse it

knowledgeChecks.question: What does a disinfectant label's contact time mean?
options: How long the bottle can be stored
How long the surface or tool must stay wet with the product
How long the client should wait before the next service

knowledgeChecks.question: Which control applies to a product used near the eyes?
options: Reading the safety data sheet and stopping if the client reports irritation
Using it on every client without checking the label
Keeping it open in the kit for the whole day
